pattern.crimePattern: a land agent who sells titles for parcels that do not exist kills the retired police sergeant who found out and gave him two days to refund
pattern.notes: Fictional agency, registry staff and parcel numbers. Mvua background: the oval seal bears the maker's mark "MV". The forgery's flaw (a parcel missing from the index map) is shown, never how a title is faked. The cultural reader is asked about the Kenyan-Asian casting (master list H, question 5).

ob.text: A land agent reports a man found dead in his inner office on the main street of Nanyuki when he arrived at 08:00. The dead man is a retired police sergeant, Kipng'eno Chepkwony (45).

reconstruction.text: Desai sells Kipng'eno a title for "parcel 2209" on the Timau road for KSh 2.8 million, with a survey Kahuthu signed for 20,000 without walking a single beacon. Hilda typed the title on a blank form, believing it was a copy.
When Kipng'eno goes to fence his plot, a farmer chases him off. Last Thursday Zablon shows him the index map: 2208, then 2210.
Monday, 18:40. Hilda goes down the stairs as Kipng'eno comes up. He gives Desai until Wednesday to refund him, or he goes to the DCI with four more parcel numbers.
Desai says he'll fetch the money. He brings the steel deed strongbox to the desk and swings its corner into Kipng'eno's head.
At 21:30 his phone leaves the office. In the morning, he "arrives and finds him", and calls his advocate before he calls the police.

afterVerdict.beat: Pattern File, t_mvua and t_stamp: "MVUA HOLDINGS — title processing", and the maker's mark on the oval seal: "MV". Amani's notebook: "An oval seal marked MV. Mvua doesn't just pay forgers. It supplies the stamps."

clockPlan.note: Three stamps, the region maximum: records on Kahuthu, records on Desai, and a warrant on Desai's house. Desai stays silent until the index map is put in front of him. Detain him after the search; the cuff trace (12 h) and the title examination (10 h) come back inside his 24 hours.
